title.rendered: The Church the Spirit Birthed: The Gospel For Today

excerpt.rendered: The Spirit who was promised has been given. The Spirit who was given has been at work. And the Spirit who has been at work still gathers a people—the church.

content.rendered:
The Spirit who was promised has been given. The Spirit who was given has been at work. And the Spirit who has been at work still gathers a people. Two weeks of walking through Pentecost ends where Acts 2 ends—with the church the Spirit birthed.

The Gospel For Today | Sunday, May 31, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“They committed themselves to the teaching of the apostles, the life together, the common meal, and the prayers. Everyone around was in awe—all those wonders and signs done through the apostles! And all the believers lived in a wonderful harmony, holding everything in common. They sold whatever they owned and pooled their resources so that each person’s need was met. They followed a daily discipline of worship in the Temple followed by meals at home, every meal a celebration, exuberant and joyful, as they praised God. People in general liked what they saw. Every day their number grew as God added those who were saved.”
Acts 2:42–47 (MSG)

Today’s Message

For two weeks we have walked the long road of the Spirit. We started with Joel, eight hundred years before Pentecost, glimpsing the day God would pour Himself out on all flesh. We walked through the upper room, the wind and the fire, the tongues and the three thousand saved. We watched the disciples step into power they did not earn and ability they did not possess. We learned that the Spirit leads us, fruits in us, seals us, intercedes for us, frees us, and dwells in us. Today the arc closes here: with the church the Spirit birthed.

Read Luke’s description in the Message slowly. Notice what spilled out of the same Spirit at work. Teaching. Life together. Common meals. Prayers. Awe. Harmony. Shared resources. Daily worship. Joyful meals. Praise. Growth. The Spirit who fell at Pentecost did not produce isolated, individualistic Christians. He produced a body. He produced a community. He produced a church.

This is the corrective for an age that wants Jesus without the body, the Spirit without the people, the salvation without the church. The same Spirit who filled you also draws you toward others He fills. The church is not a building, a program, or an organization. The church is the gathered people the Spirit was poured out on. You and I were not just saved into Christ—we were saved into His body. The two are inseparable.

Notice the joy in the picture. The MSG captures it well: “every meal a celebration, exuberant and joyful, as they praised God.” The first Christians were not solemn. They were not religious in the dull modern sense. They were people whose lives had been wrecked by grace and could not stop celebrating. The Spirit is the source of joy, and where He is gathering, there is feast.

And look at what the world saw from the outside: awe. “Everyone around was in awe.” The people who watched the early church from a distance did not see religious bureaucracy. They saw something they could not explain. Wonder. Mystery. A community whose love did not fit the categories of their society. People being added daily because they wanted what they were witnessing. The world should still see that when it looks at us.

So we end where we began. The Spirit who was promised in Joel has been poured out at Pentecost. The Spirit who was poured out at Pentecost lives in you. The Spirit who lives in you is gathering you with His people. Worship today with the body He has given you. Eat together. Pray together. Be in awe together. The fire that fell two thousand years ago is still burning, and you are part of how it spreads.

Prayer

Father, thank You for the church You birthed by Your Spirit. Thank You that I am not a solitary Christian but a member of a body that spans every nation, language, and generation. Forgive me for the moments I have tried to walk with You without walking with Your people. Knit me into the local body You have given me. Make me a giver, a receiver, and a witness. Let the world see something in the church that it cannot explain—something that draws it to You. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

I am not a solitary Christian. I am part of the church the Spirit birthed. The same Spirit who fell at Pentecost gathers me with His people. I receive my place in the body. I give my gifts to the body. The fire that fell that day still burns in us together. The world will see, and it will be drawn to Him.
